findings.issue: The new pre-save runs before local discovery-option validation in both add functions. Invalid or missing Bright Data max_items, invalid since, or incompatible Facebook modes leave an unusable subscription and cooldown on disk before any provider call. A corrected add is then rejected as already subscribed. Validate these persisted author options before saving, reusing the fetch validators.

Both paid add paths pre-save enabled=True, while import_rss_opml applies vidbeeEnabled=false only after a successful return. Failed or interrupted discovery therefore retains a disabled OPML author as enabled, allowing later scheduled paid refreshes. Pass the imported enabled flag into the initial subscription save.

The new retained Instagram subscription has an empty url until discovery succeeds. On a provider failure, export_rss_opml emits xmlUrl='', and import_rss_opml silently skips that outline, losing the retained subscription on export/import. Initialize its canonical author URL before dispatch.

summary: Fixed three retained-subscription regressions: invalid author options persisted before validation, disabled OPML imports becoming enabled on provider failure, and retained Instagram subscriptions exporting with an empty URL. Red regressions reproduced all three on f8b91f4; direct Git Bash checks passed 932 Python tests (34 skipped), 109 widget scenarios, 30 Windows-sync checks, and self-test. scripts/check_offline.py produced two WinError 87 subprocess errors; the same complete suites passed when invoked directly.
